DATA PRODUCT FRAMEWORK · EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Data products that prove they deliver what the business asked

Every stage from a business idea to a governed BigQuery table runs through one circular lifecycle, five automated gates, and a signed plain-English playback.

6 Stages
Virtuous circular loop
5 Gates
Automated quality checks
100%
Requirement-to-test trace

Signed business playback
Welcome to the Executive Summary of the Data Product Framework. In seven slides, we show how a business idea becomes a verified, governed data product in BigQuery and BigQuery Knowledge Catalog—with sample views of the Use-Case Definition, BRD/PRD, and Output Data Product.
01 · THE EXECUTIVE PROBLEM & SOLUTION

Unchecked pipelines silently drift from business rules while technical tests stay green

1 · WHAT THE BUSINESS ASKS

Plain-English commercial rules

Finance and Sales leaders ask for trusted metrics defined in business terms, not SQL code.

EXAMPLE BUSINESS RULE
“Cancelled or unfulfilled sales orders must never appear in monthly net sales.”
  • Owned and approved by the business sponsor
  • Clear rules for freshness, history, and privacy
  • Scored for value and ease before engineering starts
2 · WHERE PIPELINES FAIL

Hand-coded translations lose intent

When specs live in static slide decks and SQL is hand-written, business meaning breaks silently.

GREEN PIPELINE · WRONG REVENUE
A column check passes while amended orders are double-counted in monthly revenue.
  • Documents drift from production SQL on day two
  • Technical tests check column types, not business logic
  • Downstream consumers discover errors in board meetings
3 · HOW DPF ENFORCES TRUST

Signed playback to proven output

The framework compiles approved requirements directly into code, sandbox tests, and catalog metadata.

AUTOMATED PROOF (GATE G4)
Every requirement scenario runs against sandbox data before BigQuery views can be published.
  • Sponsor signs a plain-English business playback (G1)
  • Approved patterns generate SQL, infrastructure, and tests (G2–G3)
  • Live service breaches open a governed change proposal
Executive Guarantee: No engineering starts without a scored use case and plain-English specification (Gate G0), and no table publishes without passing every business scenario (Gate G4).
Slide 2 contrasts traditional data pipelines with the Data Product Framework. Traditional pipelines test whether columns are null; our framework proves that every business rule—like excluding cancelled orders or preserving historical customer segments—passes in sandbox before publication.
02 · THE VIRTUOUS CIRCULAR LIFECYCLE & GATE GOVERNANCE

Six stages and five machine gates: four with digest-bound HITL sign-off, one 100% automated

Solid Pill (G0, G1, G3, G4): Machine Check + Digest-Bound HITL Dashed Pill (G2 & Loop): 100% Automated Gate
STAGES 1 & 2 · DEFINE & DESIGN 2 HITL Gates · G0 & G1

Define rules, dimensional model, and playback

Sponsors score the use case and approve a plain-English BRD. In Design, the TDD resolves the Kimball star schema, SCD Type 2 history, and grains—played back in plain English.

G0 · HITL — BUSINESS OWNER
Machine checks rubric & zero jargon; Sponsor signs off BRD.
G1 · HITL — BUSINESS + ARCH
Sponsor signs semantics.md (sha256) + Architect approves TDD.
STAGES 3 & 4 · COMPOSE & BUILD 1 Auto (G2) · 1 HITL (G3)

Bind executable skills, type-check DAG, and build

Compose matches each designed model (such as SCD Type 2 dimensions and facts) to its skill and type-checks the DAG. Build renders deterministic SQL, Terraform, and tests.

G2 · AUTO ⚡ — 100% MACHINE
Zero HITL: Binds skills, type-checks 22 contracts & maps AX → AT.
G3 · HITL — ENGINEER PR DIFF
Double-builds for determinism & 100% trace; Engineer reviews Golden Copy PR.
STAGES 5 & 6 · TEST, PUBLISH & MONITOR 1 HITL (G4) · Auto Loop

Prove every scenario and guard production

Sandbox execution proves every business scenario before publishing to BigQuery and Knowledge Catalog. Live service watches automatically reopen changes on drift.

G4 · HITL — DOMAIN ATTEST
Sandbox SQL tests pass + Finance & Merchandising attest (sha256).
LOOP · AUTO ↻ — BREACH GUARD
SLA or schema breach auto-opens a change proposal back at G0 · HITL.
Why HITL Sign-Offs Never Go Stale: Every human signature at G1 (semantics.md) and G4 (dpf test attest) is bound to a cryptographic sha256 digest—if any requirement, grain, or SQL changes, the gate automatically invalidates the signature.
Slide 3 presents the circular 6-stage lifecycle and highlights the exact balance between machine gates and Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) governance. Four gates (G0, G1, G3, G4) pair automated CLI checks with human sign-off (Business Owner at G0, Business + Architect on the sha256 playback digest at G1, Engineer PR review of the Golden Copy diff at G3, and Finance/Merchandising domain attestation on the sha256 build digest at G4). Gate G2 (Compose) and the Monitor Breach Loop are 100% automated.
03 · SAMPLE ARTEFACT 1 OF 3 · STAGE 1: DEFINE

Business sponsors define and score candidate use cases before anyone writes requirements

DEFINE · STEP 1 Business Intake

1. Structured business problem & SWOT

The sponsor captures the business problem, decisions supported, corporate SWOT alignment, value drivers, and data readiness in plain business language.

DEFINE · STEP 2 107 / 170 (63%)

2. Weighted 11-criterion panel scorecard

After an automated readiness check verifies every section is complete, the cross-functional panel scores 7 Value criteria (3.05/5) and 4 Ease criteria (3.33/5).

DEFINE · STEP 3 Quick Win

3. Portfolio quadrant placement

Plotting Value against Ease places Sales Performance in the Quick Win quadrant (≥ 3.0 on both axes), unlocking approval to author the requirements.

Portfolio Discipline: Weak or unready ideas are filtered out in two pages before data engineers spend a single hour writing specifications or pipelines.
Slide 4 showcases the Use-Case Definition two-page spread, the 11-criterion Panel Scorecard, and the 2x2 Value vs Ease Prioritisation Matrix for Sales Performance.
04 · SAMPLE ARTEFACT 2 OF 3 · BRD & PRD SPECIFICATIONS

Approved use cases become plain-English BRD or PRD specs with testable scenarios

Direct Compilation to Test: Scenario AX-12 (Given a cancelled order, When figures are published, Then it is excluded from net sales) compiles directly into an automated Gate G4 test.
BUSINESS VIEW · BRD Finance & Ops

1. Business Requirements Document (BRD)

Captures purpose, metric formulas, exception handling, and commercial trade-offs (such as moving from 15-minute to hourly refresh to avoid database replication costs).

PRODUCT VIEW · PRD Same Standard

2. Product Requirements Document (PRD)

Product-led teams can use the companion PRD template (Product Summary, Users & Use Cases, Quality Bar). Both templates enforce the exact same governance rubric.

GATE G0 · 13 SCENARIOS Zero Tech Jargon

3. Testable Given / When / Then rules

Every business rule carries a concrete acceptance scenario. Gate G0 blocks the specification if it contains technical jargon like BigQuery, Dataform, or partition.

Gate G0 Enforcement: The specification must be 100% readable by a business owner while remaining structured enough to generate automated acceptance tests.
Slide 5 shows both the filled Business Requirements Document (BRD) two-page spread and the side-by-side comparison with the Product Requirements Document (PRD), plus a close-up of Requirement R-11 and its Given/When/Then scenario.
05 · SAMPLE ARTEFACT 3 OF 3 · STAGES 2–6: OUTPUT DATA PRODUCT

One manifest generates the signed business playback, governed BigQuery views, and catalog entry

PLAYBACK & PORTS Gates G1 & G4

1. Signed business playback & output ports

Shows the sponsor-signed plain-English playback alongside the three published BigQuery consumption interfaces: two internal views and one external partner share.

DATA & GOVERNANCE 9 Glossary Terms

2. Verified BigQuery rows & Knowledge Catalog

Proves point-in-time segment history (Acme Pty Ltd stays SMB in March and becomes Enterprise in June), binds 9 business glossary terms in BigQuery Knowledge Catalog, and masks PII.

RELEASE ASSURANCE 13 / 13 Passed

3. Unbroken verification & live monitoring

Publication is blocked unless the signed specification and tested sandbox build match. Live monitors enforce the 06:00 AEST daily close and 60-minute freshness target.

What Consumers Receive: Governed BigQuery views, rich business definitions in BigQuery Knowledge Catalog, masked contact PII, and guaranteed service levels.
Slide 6 presents the Output Data Product dossier: the signed business playback, the three published BigQuery output ports, verified output rows, BigQuery Knowledge Catalog glossary bindings, and policy-tag masking on customer contact fields.
06 · EXECUTIVE SUMMARY · END-TO-END ARTEFACT CHAIN

Every production figure traces back to a signed requirement and a scored business need

1 · USE-CASE DEFINITION 107/170 Quick Win

Prove the idea is worth building

Two-page business intake, 11-criterion weighted scorecard, and 2×2 portfolio matrix completed before requirements begin.

2 · BRD / PRD SPECIFICATION Gates G0 & G1

Lock testable rules in plain English

Business-language BRD or product-framed PRD with concrete Given / When / Then scenarios and zero technical jargon.

3 · OUTPUT DATA PRODUCT Gates G2 – G4

Publish verified views & catalog

Signed business playback, three governed BigQuery output ports, nine Knowledge Catalog glossary bindings, and live service monitors.

End-to-End Governance: Every data product moves from a two-page Use-Case Definition through a plain-English BRD or PRD into a verified BigQuery and Knowledge Catalog asset.
Slide 7 brings all three artefacts together side-by-side: the Use-Case Definition, the BRD/PRD Specification, and the Output Data Product dossier.
